entryPoint: Topic::isActive() in include/class.topic.php (lines 194-196): a zero-argument public instance method returning `!!($this->flags & self::FLAG_ACTIVE)`. Topic::isEnabled() (lines 190-192) is a pure delegation wrapper that immediately returns `$this->isActive()` with no added logic, so callers of either name observe identical behavior.
coreLogic: The entire logic is one inline expression: bitwise AND of the packed `flags` int against the class constant FLAG_ACTIVE (0x0002), coerced to a strict PHP boolean via the double-negation `!!` idiom (so any non-zero masked result becomes exactly `true`, not a truthy int). Topic packs three independent flag bits into the single `flags` column: FLAG_CUSTOM_NUMBERS (0x0001), FLAG_ACTIVE (0x0002), and FLAG_ARCHIVED (0x0004) — isActive() only ever inspects the FLAG_ACTIVE bit and is indifferent to the state of the other two bits. isEnabled() sits directly above isActive() in the chain and adds no logic; it exists only as an alternate public name for the same check. A separate, unrelated method, getStatus() (lines 197-204), independently re-checks the same FLAG_ACTIVE bit (plus FLAG_ARCHIVED) with a bare `&` (no boolean coercion) to produce a tri-state string ('Active'/'Archived'/'Disabled') for display — it does not call isActive() and is not part of this delegation chain, listed only as context per the acceptance criteria. Likewise, the static Topic::getHelpTopics() (line 338) independently computes `$flags & self::FLAG_ACTIVE` in a bulk list-building loop over raw ORM tuples without ever calling isActive() or isEnabled() — also out-of-chain context, not a call site to preserve.
consumers: Topic::isEnabled() (include/class.topic.php:191) — direct, logic-free delegation: `return $this->isActive();`. Any external caller of isEnabled() is transitively a consumer of isActive()'s exact boolean.

include/staff/filter.inc.php:253 — inside the filter-editor admin page, `if($topic && !$topic->isActive()) $_warn = sprintf(...)`; sets a non-fatal UI warning string shown next to a 'topic' filter action whose configured Topic is not active. Does not block saving.
scp/filters.php:150 — same warning pattern on the filter list/edit entry page: `if($topic && !$topic->isActive()) $warn = sprintf(...)`, informational only.

include/class.ticket.php:3686 (Ticket::update() field validation) — `$topic = Topic::lookup($vars['topicId']); if($topic && !$topic->isActive()) $errors['topicId'] = ...`; a falsy isActive() result on a topic being assigned during a ticket update produces a hard validation error, blocking the update.

include/class.ticket.php:4214 (Ticket::create() validation, direct topicId branch) — `if (is_numeric($vars['topicId']) && ($topic=Topic::lookup((int)$vars['topicId'])) && $topic->isActive()) { ...apply topic forms... } else { $vars['topicId'] = 0; }`; a falsy result silently resets the requested topicId to 0 rather than raising an error (asymmetric with the update() path above).

include/class.ticket.php:4269 (Ticket::create() validation, email-derived topic fallback inside the emailId branch) — `if (!isset($topic) && ($T = $email->getTopic()) && ($T->isActive())) { $topic = $T; }`; a falsy result on the email's configured topic simply skips the fallback (topic stays unset), it is not surfaced as an error.

include/class.filter_action.php:536 (FA_AssignTopic::apply(), executed when a matching filter fires on a ticket) — `if ($config['topic_id']) { $topic = Topic::lookup($config['topic_id']); if ($topic && $topic->isActive()) $ticket['topicId'] = $config['topic_id']; }`; a falsy result means the filter action is silently skipped and the ticket's topic is left unmodified.

include/class.filter_action.php:561 (FA_AssignTopic::getConfigurationOptions(), admin UI for editing a filter action) — inverted usage: `if ($topic && !$topic->isActive()) $choices[$topic->getId()] = $topic->getName();`; explicitly re-adds an already-configured-but-now-inactive topic into the picklist so the admin can still see/keep the existing (inactive) selection, rather than having it silently disappear from the dropdown.

include/class.filter.php:646 (filter-action save/validation routine) — `if (!$topic || !$topic->isActive()) { $errors['err'] = sprintf(__('Unable to save: Please choose an active %s'), 'Help Topic'); }`; a falsy result is a hard save-blocking validation error for a 'topic' type filter action.

include/class.config.php:1427 (Config::updateTicketsSettings()) — `if ($vars['default_help_topic'] && ($T = Topic::lookup($vars['default_help_topic'])) && !$T->isActive()) { $errors['default_help_topic'] = __('Default help topic must be set to active'); }`; a falsy result blocks saving the system-wide default help topic setting.

Verified NOT consumers of this Topic method despite matching a bare `->isActive()`/`->isEnabled()` grep: Dept::isActive(), SLA::isActive(), Staff::isActive(), Plugin::isActive(), Filter::isActive(), Team::isActive()/isEnabled(), User/Collaborator::isActive(), Canned::isEnabled(), DynamicFormField/DynamicForm::isEnabled(), ApiKey::isActive() — all are same-named methods on unrelated classes. Also excluded: scp/helptopics.php:236 and include/class.topic.php:442, which both call ->isActive() on a Dept object obtained via $topic->getDept(), not on the Topic itself.
inputShape: None. isActive() takes zero parameters. Its sole implicit input is $this->flags (int), the packed bitmask column already present in memory on the Topic instance as loaded by the ORM (VerySimpleModel) — isActive() performs no lazy-load, no fetch, and reads nothing else.
outputShape: A strict PHP boolean produced by double-negating (`!!`) the bitwise-AND of $this->flags against Topic::FLAG_ACTIVE (0x0002): true when the FLAG_ACTIVE bit is set in flags (regardless of whether FLAG_CUSTOM_NUMBERS or FLAG_ARCHIVED bits are also set), false when it is not set — including when flags is 0. Because `&` (not `&&`) is used, this is a correct, precise single-bit check, distinct from the logical-AND `&&` quirk found in other tickets' seams (e.g. MOD-26) — this method has no such bug to preserve/replicate; the extraction must keep the bitwise semantics exact. isEnabled() returns the identical boolean via pure delegation.
sideEffects: None. No DB reads or writes are performed by isActive() or isEnabled().
No global state ($cfg or otherwise) is read or written.
No lazy-loading or caching is triggered — flags is a scalar property already populated on the object by the ORM before isActive() runs.
No mutation of $this or of any parameter (there are none) — the call is a pure read.
constraints: Preserve the bitwise `&` operator and the FLAG_ACTIVE = 0x0002 mask exactly; do not substitute logical `&&`, a different bit, or a different flags column.

Preserve the `!!` double-negation so the return value is a strict PHP boolean (true/false), not a truthy/falsy int (e.g. the raw masked int 2), to keep byte-for-byte caller-visible behavior (loose (==) and strict (===) comparisons against true/false must both keep working identically).

Topic::isActive()'s method signature (zero args) and Topic::isEnabled()'s pure delegation to it must remain unchanged on the facade after the strangler patch — isEnabled() must keep calling isActive() (or the same underlying check) and must not independently duplicate or diverge from the extracted logic.

The extracted service must accept the raw `flags` int (or equivalent primitive) as a plain parameter, not the Topic object, and must never call back into Topic::isActive() or Topic::isEnabled() (anti-recursion) or into any other Topic instance method.

Must not alter the independent, out-of-chain flag reads in Topic::getStatus() or the static Topic::getHelpTopics() — those are separate, pre-existing bitwise checks on the same constant and are explicitly out of scope for this facade patch.

Do not touch include/class.sla.php, include/class.dept.php, include/class.team.php, or include/class.ticket.php — those files' own isActive()/isEnabled() methods (SLA, Dept, Team) and their Topic::isActive() call sites (class.ticket.php) are consumers to document only, not to edit; Ticket's own overdue/assignment logic is out of scope entirely.

flags values with FLAG_ACTIVE unset but other bits set (e.g. FLAG_ARCHIVED alone, or FLAG_ARCHIVED+FLAG_CUSTOM_NUMBERS combined) must continue to return false; flags with FLAG_ACTIVE set combined with any other bit(s) must continue to return true — the method is indifferent to all bits except FLAG_ACTIVE.
harnessInputShape: JSON input has a single field: flags (int) — the raw Topic bitmask value to set directly on an in-memory Topic object's `flags` property (e.g. via Topic::create()/property assignment, without saving to the DB, since isActive() only reads the in-process property and has no other side effects to capture) before calling isActive() (and, to prove the delegation, isEnabled()) and recording the boolean return value. Use flags=2 for the 'active' fixture (FLAG_ACTIVE alone); flags=0 or flags=1 (FLAG_CUSTOM_NUMBERS alone, FLAG_ACTIVE bit absent) for 'inactive'; flags=4 (FLAG_ARCHIVED alone, FLAG_ACTIVE bit absent) for 'archived-only'; and flags=7 or flags=3 (FLAG_ACTIVE combined with FLAG_ARCHIVED and/or FLAG_CUSTOM_NUMBERS) for 'active-plus-other-flags', which must still return true since only the FLAG_ACTIVE bit is inspected.
